articles.title: Lucélia Albuquerque, fundadora do Guerreiros do Passo, morre no Recife | G1
articles.standfirst: Coletivo recifense ganhou fama internacional ao desfilar em Cannes com elenco de 'O Agente Secreto', em 2025. Dançarina lutava contra câncer na medula havia sete anos.
articles.summary: Dançarina tinha 44 anos e lutava contra câncer na medula havia sete anos. Grupo ganhou fama internacional ao desfilar em Cannes com elenco de 'O Agente Secreto'.
articles.body:
Morreu no Recife , na madrugada deste domingo (8) a professora e passista de frevo Lucélia Albuquerque, uma das fundadoras do Guerreiros do Passo, grupo de frevo que se tornou Patrimônio Cultural do Recife e ganhou fama internacional ao desfilar no Festival de Cannes com o elenco do filme "O Agente Secreto" (veja vídeo acima) .

Segundo a família, a morte de Lucélia foi confirmada por volta da 1h20. Ela tinha 44 anos e fazia tratamento havia sete anos contra o mieloma múltiplo, um tipo de câncer que se origina na medula óssea. O velório é realizado na Casa Batista, no bairro de Santo Amaro, no Centro do Recife. O enterro está marcado para as 15h, no Cemitério de Santo Amaro.

Ao g1 , o viúvo de Lucélia e também fundador do grupo, Eduardo Araújo, contou que ela estava internada desde o dia 30 de outubro no Hospital da Unimed, no bairro da Ilha do Leite, na região central da capital pernambucana.

"Ela vinha lutando contra a doença, passando por vários protocolos, mas não deram os resultados que a equipe médica esperava. Ela foi lutando, mas era uma rotina muito pesada e cansativa e, agora, de fato, ela descansou", disse.

Lucélia e Eduardo estavam juntos havia mais de 20 anos. Os dois se conheceram na Escola Municipal de Frevo do Recife. Professora de artes da prefeitura, ela também atuava como passista no Guerreiros do Passo. Nas apresentações do grupo, a artista interpretava uma personagem caracterizada como uma mulher de época, com vestido listrado.

"Lucélia sempre comigo, em manada, em parceria, companheira, participando das ações do grupo. Ela é professora também, pesquisadora. Ela comigo fundou vários projetos dentro do Guerreiros, projetos de pesquisa. Depois ela se tornou a produtora oficial do grupo, pleiteando recursos em editais públicos para ajudar na manutenção das atividades do grupo", contou.

Lucélia Albuquerque, integrante do grupo de frevo Guerreiros do Passo — Foto: Divulgação/Acervo pessoal

Em maio de 2025, o Guerreiros do Passo ganhou destaque internacional ao participar da estreia do filme "O Agente Secreto", dirigido por Kleber Mendonça Filho e protagonizado por Wagner Moura, durante o Festival de Cannes , na França. O longa conquistou dois prêmios na edição do evento.

O grupo também participou de uma sessão especial do filme no Palácio da Alvorada, em Brasília, a convite do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e da primeira-dama Janja da Silva. A exibição foi chamada de "Cine Alvorada".

"Foi um ano muito bom para o grupo, a gente viajou para a Europa, viajou pelo Brasil. Quando ela chegava, nos intervalos das viagens, de alguma missão, ia para o hospital fazer o tratamento dela. (...) Era uma rotina muito pesada e cansativa", contou.

Segundo Eduardo, a participação nas atividades do grupo ajudava Lucélia a enfrentar o tratamento e, mesmo diante das dificuldades, ela mantinha os planos para o futuro e a disposição de continuar realizando projetos ligados ao frevo.

"A gente ficava ali dentro do universo do frevo, também utilizando essa atuação como uma forma de terapia. Porque, saindo dali, a gente voltava para o hospital fazer tratamento. [...] Ela nunca esmorecia. Tinha uma vontade de viver incrível, uma vontade de fazer as coisas, de realizar. A gente já estava planejando coisas para esse ano que vem. É uma pessoa brilhante, tem uma luz intensa. Sempre foi parceira comigo", declarou.

"Guerreiros do Passo" no Palácio da Alvorada, em Brasília, durante evento para exibição do filme "O Agente Secreto" — Foto: Divulgação/Ricardo Stuckert

A Secretaria de Cultura de Pernambuco (Secult) e a prefeitura do Recife lamentaram a morte de Lucélia e destacaram a contribuição da artista para a preservação e a celebração do frevo, uma das principais expressões da identidade cultural pernambucana.

"Lucélia fez do frevo sua expressão de vida, levando aos corpos, às ruas e à memória coletiva a força, a alegria e a resistência dessa manifestação tão representativa da nossa cultura. Sua dança ajudou a manter viva a tradição e a beleza do frevo, patrimônio cultural de Pernambuco", afirma a nota da Secult.

Já a prefeitura do Recife destacou sua dedicação à salvaguarda da manifestação cultural.

"De hoje em diante, todos os nossos passos voarão ao encontro de Lucélia Albuquerque, passista, atriz, professora, integrante e umas das fundadoras do grupo Guerreiros do Passo, que devotou sua alegria, sua luta de todos os dias e todos os seus voos, até o derradeiro, à salvaguarda e à celebração do frevo", disse.

articles.title: Maestra da própria obra, Marisa Monte rege sinfonia de 'Phonica', show que se conserva perfeito um ano após a estreia | G1
articles.body:
Marisa Monte reapresenta o show 'Phonica' na Brava Arena Jockey, na cidade natal do Rio de Janeiro (RJ) — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

♬ Quando Marisa Monte terminou de cantar “Ainda bem” (2011), parceria com Arnaldo Antunes, a artista foi ovacionada pelo público que lotou as pistas e camarotes da Brava Arena Jockey na noite de ontem, sábado, 7 de novembro, para assistir à segunda das três últimas apresentações de “Phonica” no Rio de Janeiro (RJ) na volta do show sinfônico à cidade natal de Marisa, um ano após a chegada do concerto pop ao Rio em 31 de outubro de 2025.

A ovação foi tão grande que cantora e orquestra tiveram que paralisar o show por alguns segundos para Marisa receber os aplausos do público. Situação semelhante aconteceria, sete números depois, quando a cantora terminou de dar voz à apaixonante balada “Depois” (2011), outra parceria de Marisa com Arnaldo e, no caso, também com Carlinhos Brown.

Curiosamente, tanto “Ainda bem” quanto “Depois” são músicas de álbum, “O que você quer saber de verdade” (2011), recebido com certa frieza no lançamento por parte de uma crítica que não soube detectar de imediato a força perene do cancioneiro autoral apresentado por Marisa Monte naquele grande disco...

Em essência, pouco mais de um ano após a estreia nacional da turnê em Belo Horizonte (MG), em 18 de novembro de 2025, “Phonica” se conserva grandioso e perfeito em cena. E, se a orquestra atua sob a batuta certeira do maestro André Bachur, quem rege o concerto e a devoção do público é a própria Marisa Monte , maestra da própria obra e da carreira iniciada em outubro de 1987.

Marisa Monte segue roteiro de 27 músicas na volta do show 'Phonica' ao Rio de Janeiro (RJ) e oferece bônus após o bis — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

Ali, no palco da Brava Arena Jockey, estava mais uma vez uma senhora cantora e uma senhora compositora, autora (com parceiros como Arnaldo Antunes, Carlinhos Brown e Nando Reis) de 18 das 27 músicas de um roteiro que, no show de ontem, teve o acréscimo de versão a capella de “Bem que se quis” (“E po' che fà” – Pino Danielle, 1982, em versão em português de Nelson Motta, 1989), bônus que volta e meia Marisa oferece ao público cativo desde o show “Memórias, crônicas e declarações de amor” (2000).

Até os inesperados tropeços da cantora nas letras de “O que você quer saber de verdade” ( Marisa Monte , Arnaldo Antunes e Carlinhos Brown, 2006) e “Infinito particular” ( Marisa Monte , Arnaldo Antunes e Carlinhos Brown, 2006), foram encarados com naturalidade pela maestra, ciente de que ninguém é regente da vida. “A vida é assim. Nada sob controle”, gracejou a artista após o canto de “Infinito particular”.

Prestes a completar 60 anos de vida e 40 de carreira em 2027, efemérides que não deverão passar em branco ao longo do próximo ano, Marisa Monte consegue se impor naturalmente, sem afetação ou ares de superioridade, diante da orquestra comandada por Bachur.

Todo mundo vê e sente que é ela, Marisa, a delicada regente da sinfonia pop de “Phonica” , show que merecia ser perpetuado em registro audiovisual pela beleza do concerto e dos arranjos criados por Ubiratan Marques (maestro da Orquestra Afrosinfônica, da Bahia), o violinista Newton Carneiro e os pianistas Thiago Costa, Débora Gurgel e Jether Garotti para embalar um repertório majoritariamente autoral que reforça a assinatura imprimida por Marisa Monte na música brasileira há 35 anos, precisamente desde 1991, ano em que a cantora começou a gravar as próprias músicas no álbum “Mais” .

Enfim, “Phonica” representa o triunfo dessa obra ora enquadrada em moldura orquestral, em interseção com a linguagem da música erudita, sem diluição do apelo pop.

Marisa Monte e o maestro André Bachur saúdam o público ao fim da apresentação do concerto pop 'Phonica' na Brava Arena Jockey — Foto: Rodrigo Goffredo

articles.title: Festival de Serra de São Bento recebe Vanessa da Mata, Dorgival e SPC | G1
articles.standfirst: Após adiamento, evento comemora 15 anos com programação de quinta-feira (12) a domingo (15), na cidade de Serra de São Bento.
articles.summary: Após adiamento, evento comemora 15 anos com programação de quinta-feira (12) a domingo (15), na cidade de Serra de São Bento.
articles.body:
A edição 2026 do Festival Multicultural de Serra de São Bento será realizado de quinta (12) a domingo (15), com a presença de atrações nacionais como Vanessa da Mata, Dorgival Dantas, Henry Freitas e Só Pra Contrariar. O acesso é gratuito.

O festival celebra 15 anos de existência em 2026 e a expectativa da organização é que a cidade de Serra de São Bento receba mais de 70 mil pessoas ao longo dos quatro dias de programação. Municípios vizinhos também se movimentam para receber visitantes.

A noite de abertura, na quinta-feira (12), será dedicada à música gospel, com o pastor Roberto Pontes, o Ministério de Louvor Sublime Trono e Canção & Louvor.

Dorgival Dantas se apresenta no Festival Multicultural de Serra de São Bento — Foto: Bruna Couto/g1

Vanessa da Mata, Henry Freitas, Raynel Guedes e Mercinho sobem ao palco na sexta-feira (13).

No sábado (14) tem Só Pra Contrariar, Dorgival Dantas e Katia & Aduílio, além da Banda Cítrika.

O encerramento no domingo (15) contará com shows de João Marcos e Banda, César Soanata e Banda Zaya.

"A valorização de talentos locais e de estados vizinhos garante visibilidade a artistas que raramente ocupam palcos de grande porte na região", afirmou Diel Figueiredo, secretário de Turismo de Serra de São Bento.

Além da arena principal dos shows, o Festival terá praça turística com apresentação de mais de 25 bandas regionais, que começam de manhã e vão até as 22h. A feira gastronômica e a exposição de artesanato também integram a programação.

O Festival de Serra de São Bento seria realizado entre 31 de julho e 2 de agosto, mas foi adiado por conta do bloqueio de repasses federais , ocasionado pelas eleições.

articles.title: 'Ramayana: Rise of a Legend': Ranbir Kapoor's stunt double Luke Ioannou shares unseen set pictures; says, 'Feeling incredibly privileged'
articles.summary: Stunt performer Luke Ioannou has shared a collection of behind-the-scenes photographs from the sets of Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Part 1'.
articles.body: Stunt performer Luke Ioannou has shared a collection of behind-the-scenes photographs from the sets of Nitesh Tiwari's 'Ramayana: Part 1'. The pictures offer a glimpse into the production of the upcoming mythological epic. Luke also revealed that he worked as Ranbir Kapoor's stunt double for the film. Alongside the photographs, he posted a heartfelt note about his experience and praised the actor's professionalism.Luke has worked on several major international productions, including 'Wonder Woman', 'Wonder Woman 1984' and 'No Time to Die'. His involvement in 'Ramayana: Part 1' has now brought attention to the action team's contribution to the ambitious project. The photographs also offer a look at some of the costumes, equipment and setups used during filming.Luke Ioannou reveals he doubled for Ranbir Kapoor in 'Ramayana'Luke expressed how meaningful it was to contribute to a film based on an important Indian epic. He also spoke about his experience of working alongside Ranbir Kapoor, describing the actor in glowing terms. Sharing the pictures on Instagram, the stunt performer wrote, “Feeling incredibly privileged to have been part of telling such an important story on Ramayana, stunt doubling for Ranbir Kapoor, truly one of the best actors I've had the pleasure of working with.”Stunt performer thanks Ian Van Temperley and G Stunt Alliance GroupLuke also used the post to acknowledge the people who helped him become part of the production. He specifically thanked Ian Van Temperley and the G Stunt Alliance Group for providing the opportunity. The performer extended his appreciation to the cast and crew members who worked with him throughout the shoot.Reflecting on the experience, Luke added, “An unforgettable journey, and truly humbled to have been a part of it.” His message conveyed his appreciation for being involved in a project that brings the epic to the screen on a large scale.Unseen pictures offer a glimpse of costumes and action arrangementsThe photographs shared by Luke reveal some of the visual details behind the film's production. One picture shows a performer standing beside Ranbir Kapoor in a golden-brown traditional outfit. The costume features multiple layers of rudraksha beads, while the performer's hair is styled in a topknot.Another image focuses on an elaborate costume comprising a leather-like chest piece and a maroon dhoti. Artificial rocky formations appear in the background, offering a glimpse of the environment constructed for the shoot. These details provide an indication of the visual preparation involved in recreating the epic's world.Mechanical creature and blue-screen setup reveal scale of action sequencesThe action-related photographs offer another look at the production's technical arrangements. One image features a stunt performer standing on a large mechanical rig designed to resemble a mythical creature. Multiple wires are attached to the structure, which is positioned against a blue-screen backdrop.A separate photograph captures a massive camera rig arranged for filming. The equipment highlights the technical coordination required to shoot elaborate action sequences. Together, these images offer a rare look at the work that takes place behind the camera on a large-scale fantasy production.'Ramayana: Part 1' collects Rs 375.50 cr worldwide in three daysMeanwhile, 'Ramayana: Part 1' has recorded a strong opening at the box office. Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the mythological drama features Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi in prominent roles. The film witnessed a substantial increase in collections on Saturday, its third day in theatres.According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs 69.80 cr in India net collections on Saturday. The amount came from 23,696 shows nationwide, marking a 45.3% increase over the previous day's earnings. Its cumulative India net collection has reached Rs 182.70 cr, while the domestic gross stands at Rs 218.25 cr.The film's worldwide gross collection has climbed to Rs 375.50 cr within its first three days. articles.title: 'Ramayana' box office collection day 4 (LIVE): The Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi starrer crosses Rs 230 crore net in India, Diwali, Laxmi Puja to play key role in determining Sunday numbers
articles.summary: ‘Ramayana: Part I’, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash among others, has maintained its strong momentum at the Indian box office on its first
articles.body: ‘Ramayana: Part I’, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash among others, has maintained its strong momentum at the Indian box office on its first Sunday. The film released on November 5, Thursday while it dropped on day 2, Friday, the growth on Saturday was quite encouraging. The Sunday numbers further show significant jump over its collections at the same time on each of its previous three days. With day 4 coinciding with Diwali and Lakshmi Puja, the film's evening business could face some pressure as festivities are likely to keep a section of moviegoers occupied.A comparison of its day-wise performance at the corresponding reporting time highlights the film's steady growth. ‘Ramayana’ had collected Rs 64.85 crore net on its day 1. It saw a drop of around 25 percent on day 2, which is Friday bringing its second day total to Rs 48 crore net. On Saturday, it made more than the first day, with Rs 69.80crore. On Sunday, till evening the film has collected Rs 47.83 crore. The total net collection in India now stands at Rs 230.53 crore.Day wise collection of 'Ramayana: Part 1'Day 1 (Thursday) - Rs 64.85 croreDay 2 (Friday) - Rs 48.05 croreDay 3 (Saturday) - Rs 69.80 croreDay 4 (Sunday) LIVE - Rs 47.83 croreTotal net collection in India - Rs 230.53 croreThe Sunday trend comes after the film registered its biggest single-day collection on Saturday, earning Rs. 67.80 crore nett. Its strong start on Day 4 indicates sustained audience interest, although the eventual collection will depend on how well it holds up during the evening.Diwali and Lakshmi Puja could, however, prove to be a key factor in determining the film's final Sunday total. The evening is traditionally reserved for prayers and celebrations, with families attending pujas at home and visiting friends and relatives. This can affect theatrical footfalls even for films enjoying strong audience interest. It remains to be seen whether ‘Ramayana’ can sustain its momentum despite the festive-day challenge.Karnataka and Maharashtra have emerged as the leading contributors to the film's Sunday collections so far, with Bengaluru and Mumbai among its strongest-performing cities.'Ramayana' is directed by Nitesh Tiwari.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Gonzalo Bernardos, economista, critica la huelga general y se enzarza con Afra Blanco: "Por primera vez en el mundo hay una prospectiva"
articles.standfirst: El profesor universitario critica con severidad a los sindicatos
articles.summary: El profesor universitario critica con severidad a los sindicatos
articles.body: El economista Gonzalo Bernardos se ha mostrado muy crítico con la huelga general convocada para este próximo miércoles, 11 de noviembre. El profesor universitario, en 'La Sexta Xplica', ha criticado esta medida de presión social. "Por primera vez en la historia, una asociación que no sabemos quién la financia ni cuánta gente tiene afiliada va a convocar una huelga. Y la huelga es convocada por 'a ver qué sucede'. Es prácticamente para que no venga el Partido Popular porque 'uy lo que va a poder hacer'. Es una huelga prospectiva", ha comentado durante su turno de palabra. Gonzalo Bernardos, por otra parte, ha valorado el papel de los sindicatos: "Han sido muy importantes para generar una mayor igualdad, pero yo estoy decepcionadísimo con los sindicatos. Ya lo estoy desde que apoyaron el derecho a decidir en Cataluña por cobrar las subvenciones de la Generalitat". El economista ha denunciado, según ha explicado, las subvenciones que reciben los sindicatos por parte del gobierno. "Y atención, señores, ¿qué se puede hacer con 155 millones? Es la subvención que se ha dado a las organizaciones sindicales el Ministerio de Trabajo. En 2018 daba 8,8 millones y ahora da 32 millones. Los grandes beneficiados en 2025, UGT y Comisiones Obreras", ha manifestado. Gonzalo Bernardos, tras plantear este dato, ha cuestionado el papel de estas organizaciones: "Los sindicatos, con esta convocatoria de huelga, indiscutiblemente se han desprestigiado. Y quiero dejar muy claro que han hecho mucho, pero que los actuales dirigentes lo que hacen es un desprestigio". Afra Blanco no ha tardado en responder a las palabras del economista catalán: "Se me hinchado lo que ya no suena y lo digo así de claro. Las organizaciones sindicales tienen más afiliados que los partidos políticos. Cachondeos los justos. Lo que está diciendo el señor Bernardos es que un trabajador cuando se vaya directamente a una oferta de empleo, si no está sindicado, se negocio su sueldo, sus vacaciones, sus descansos, sus jornadas, sus planes de igualdad... Esto no pasa porque las negocian las organizaciones sindicales".

articles.title: Pierce Brosnan backs 'Fantastic Beasts' star for next James Bond, predicts fans will be 'blown away'
articles.summary: Pierce Brosnan singled out Callum Turner as a standout among the actors being considered for the next James Bond role in a Vanity Fair interview.
articles.body: Pierce Brosnan is throwing in his two cents into the conversation regarding who should be chosen to play the next James Bond, nearly 25 years after he last played the iconic character. During a recent interview with Vanity Fair, the 73-year-old actor said he is following along with the public as "an audience member," adding he is just as "eager" as everyone else "to see who is going to play this epic role of cinematic history." He did however give one actor a special shout out. "All the men who are on the list now are actors I admire," he said. "Callum, Callum Turner is someone I’ve worked with, and he’s so strong. They all have a voice and a physique, and a presence on film. They all have longevity as actors, all of these young men." While he doesn't know who will take on the iconic role next, Brosnan wishes whoever is chosen "the very best of life and strength and courage." FORMER BOND GIRL SAYS NEXT 007 SHOULD BE 'ANOTHER GORGEOUS MAN' AS JAMES BOND DECISION Brosnan first appeared as agent 007 in the 1995 movie, "GoldenEye," having taken over the reigns from Timothy Dalton. He appeared in his final Bond movie in 2002 with the release of "Die Another Day," and was replaced by Daniel Craig in the 2006 movie, "Casino Royale." Craig starred as James Bond in six films, before hanging up his badge following the release of "No Time to Die" in 2021. "You know, it’s hard to tell who it would be, but I eagerly await to hear the news and the celebration of the next James Bond," Brosnan said. In addition to a new actor playing Bond, the film is also getting a new director in Denis Villeneuve, who will be taking over the franchise, which excites Brosnan. articles.title: The OG Sita Dipika Chikhlia reacts to Sai Pallavi's combat sequences in 'Ramayana': 'I don't remember such scenes in Valmiki or Tulsidas’ Ramayana'
articles.summary: Sai Pallavi’s portrayal of Sita in Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana: Part One’ has become a talking point, particularly after glimpses of the character
articles.body: Sai Pallavi’s portrayal of Sita in Nitesh Tiwari’s ‘Ramayana: Part One’ has become a talking point, particularly after glimpses of the character participating in action sequences surfaced online. While some viewers have welcomed this interpretation, others have questioned whether it aligns with the versions of the epic they have grown up watching and reading. Amid the debate, Dipika Chikhlia, who immortalised Sita in Ramanand Sagar’s iconic 1987 television series ‘Ramayan’, has now shared her perspective on the matter.Speaking about the sequence, Dipika admitted that she could not recall coming across similar descriptions in the versions of the epic she was familiar with. articles.summary: Todo comenzó porque Pedro Sánchez recomendó una canción del grupo liderado por el difunto artista
articles.body: Los partidos políticos se encuentran sumidos en plena lucha pre elecciones generales, que tienen lugar el próximo 29 de noviembre. PSOE y PP son las dos grandes formaciones que tratarán de formar gobierno, aunque, las últimas encuestas colocan a Vox mucho más cerca de ellos de lo que parece. Pero antes de votar, tienen lugar las campañas electorales. Este domingo, 8 de noviembre, Pedro Sánchez, tras el mitin dado en Bilbao, País Vasco, en el Palacio Euskalduna, usó una canción de Extremoduro para alentar a sus seguidores: “Siempre habrá música”, publicó en X, añadiendo un link de Spotify que redirigía a la canción ‘Ama, ama, ama y ensancha el alma’, de la banda dirigida por el difunto Robe Iniesta. A esto ha contestado el Partido Popular (PP), respondiendo directamente al post: “De Extremoduro también es buena la de ‘So payaso’, Pedro”, incluso algunos de sus seguidores dieron ideas como el tema ‘Puta’. Pero la cosa no quedó aquí, ya que los socialistas contestaron: “No os habéis leído la letra”, fue lo que dijeron, enviándoles la letra completa de la canción en la publicación. Sin embargo, esto no ha gustado a muchos, que no han dudado en pedir que no se use la memoria de Robe, fallecido el pasado 10 de diciembre de 2025, para atacarse entre sí. Uno de los posts anónimos que contestaron a estas publicaciones decía: “Robe Iniesta, el líder de Extremoduro, mantuvo a lo largo de su carrera una postura escéptica y crítica con la política institucional en general, sin casarse con ninguna sigla, incluido el PSOE. El músico siempre defendió su independencia y evitó que los partidos utilizaran su figura o sus canciones con fines partidistas”, recibiendo varios ‘me gusta’. Otro, apuntó: “No entiendo muy bien que, sabiendo que a Robe no le gustaría estar en tuit de ningún partido, hagáis esto, al menos podríais respetar la memoria de los que ya no están”.

articles.summary: Bill Murray played bartender on Halloween night, pouring perfect pints of Guinness for cheering fans at a bar in Yonkers and posing for photos.
articles.body: Bill Murray was spotted enjoying Halloween in Yonkers, New York, where he interacted with fans while working behind the bar. The 76-year-old actor and former "Saturday Night Live" star was photographed sitting with Rory Dolan, the owner of Rory Dolan's Restaurant & Bar, and showing off his bartending skills by pouring Guinness for customers. The actor looked like a natural behind the bar as fans cheered when he poured a glass of Guinness. "He had a bottle of wine, a very nice bottle of wine, and he also had, he was drinking some beer, but he did pour a pint of Guinness," Dolan told Fox News Digital. "Three-part pour, which is good to see him doing it. It wasn't his first time to do it!" ACTOR BILL MURRAY STUNS TRUMP'S TOP ECONOMIC ADVISOR WITH BIZARRE QUESTION ON NEWS SHOW According to Dolan, Murray arrived at the restaurant on his own. Murray kept it casual in a black outfit, with a navy blue button-up vest over a long-sleeved black shirt. In addition to serving drinks, Murray took time to pose for photos with other patrons at the bar. "I think because he really was looking for the Irish culture," Dolan said. "He had been in Ireland doing this show. He has an excellent show out, but he was building on that energy, and he wanted to get behind the bar, pour a pint, and he wanted to know all about me and Rory Dolan's and whatever else. He was just very inquisitive, and he was very, very gracious to all, every one of the customers who went up and asked for photographs and spoke to them at length, and he was just, it was just great to have him." Dolan also shared that the restaurant was celebrating another patron's 90th birthday the night Murray visited. "The 90th birthday was that evening and then the crowd was in before the 90th birthday," Dolan said. "There was a big funeral, and they all came out to the bar, and it was just, the place was full and he was loving it." Dolan said other celebrities, including Pierce Brosnan, have also visited the bar. Murray got his big break when he was cast on "Saturday Night Live" in 1977, winning an Emmy for his work on the show's writing staff. He went on to receive an Academy Award nomination, seven Golden Globe nominations with one win, four Emmy nominations with two wins and a BAFTA Award. In his new docuseries, "A Course Called Ireland," Murray discussed his relationship to fame and whether being a public figure makes him happy, answering, "In a word, no." "It's not easy," he said, according to People. "I go through new revelations all the time about how I handle it and how to deal with it. It's not for everyone, but it has also brought me to this place, you know." Despite it not being easy, Murray also admitted that being recognized in public has brought him joy on occasion, most notably when fans share with him how much one of his films means to them. articles.title: SNL has a new impression of Elon Musk, ‘the worst thing South Africa has ever done’
articles.summary: SNL seems to have its knives out for tech executives.
articles.body:
Saturday Night Live cast member Jeremy Culhane unveiled his impression of Elon Musk last night, depicting the SpaceX and Tesla CEO as an awkward loser who fumbles his attempt to befriend the hosts of Weekend Update.

This isn’t the first time the show has lampooned the world’s richest man ( and one-time SNL host ), with Mike Myers dropping by occasionally to wield a chainsaw before freezing and muttering, “Glitch!”

Since Musk was in the news this week for spending half a billion dollars on candidates who lost in the midterms , then announcing plans to halt Cybertruck production , it’s maybe not surprising that Culhane’s version is a little less obnoxious and a little more desperate to be liked, doing his best to laugh off his setbacks and remind the audience, “ My car did a flip !”

Eventually, Weekend Update co-host Colin Jost asks a pointed question about Musk’s week: “You moved to Texas because California was run by Democrats. You moved all your companies to Texas because you didn’t want to pay taxes. You even built your own town in Texas. And now Texas is run by Democrats. Now you’re going to have to pay taxes. So how does that make you feel?”

Culhane nods along with each step of the question, then answers, “Bad?”

To show that he’s a good sport about all this, Culhane also asks his chatbot Grok to do “an epic vulgar roast of me, Elon Musk.” Grok delivers, describing Musk as “the worst thing South Africa has ever done” and suggesting, “Maybe if you have 100 more kids, one of them will talk to you .”

This week’s episode also featured a spoof of the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything,” featuring Jane Wickline’s uncanny take on the Theranos founder (though most of the jokes focus on episode host Druski).

SNL seems to have its knives out for tech executives this season, starting with Wickline’s impression of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei as a stuttering prophet of AI doom.

A couple weeks later, James Austin Johnson caricatured data center backer/”Marty Supreme” co-star Kevin O’Leary . Asked about the widespread public opposition to data centers, Johnson-as-O’Leary smoothly replies, “All I want is to buy up 40,000 acres of God’s untouched splendor and replace it with a very loud computer that steals your job.”

articles.title: Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler make blink-and-you’ll-miss-em cameos on “SNL”
articles.summary: The Druski-hosted episode also pulled appearances from Emma Stone, Walton Goggins, Dave Chappelle, and more.
articles.body:
Miami Vice '85 stars Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler made a brief cameo on the Nov. 7 edition of Saturday Night Live.

The stars appeared during the closing segment of the Druski-hosted episode.

The SNL goodnights also saw Emma Stone, Walton Goggins, Dave Chappelle, and Chris Rock take to the stage.

Studio 8H was overflowing with stars at the end of Druski's hosting debut .

After the comedian made history as the first digital content creator to host Saturday Night Live , he bid farewell to the crowd while backed by an impressive roster of A-listers. Not only was he flanked on either side by two SNL legends (we'll get to them in a second), eagle-eyed fans may have noticed that among the celebs standing onstage were Miami Vice '85 stars Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler .

Jordan and Butler, who are currently filming the Joseph Kosinski neo-noir in New York and New Jersey, showed up for a blink-and-you-miss-it cameo, hanging out in the background behind cast members and guests during the SNL goodnights. Jordan can be seen applauding from the second row while Butler stood further back and was harder to spot beneath a baseball cap.

Standing beside Druski, front and center, was SNL alum Chris Rock and four-time host Dave Chapelle, who has been known to pop in for the end of the show. Their presence came as a surprise to Druski, who was bidding the audience farewell when they showed up to embrace him.

"Oh man," Druski exclaimed. "Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock! Oh my God!"

Also amongst the crowd were Emma Stone, Walton Goggins, and newly-elected Texas senator James Talerico, who all cameoed during the episode. Druski shouted each of them out during his final remarks before turning to embrace Rock and Chappelle once again. Afterwards, Jordan emerged from the crowd, much to Druski's shock and delight.

The social media star stumbled at the sight of Jordan, who embraced him as well.

Set to the jazzy theme song, the closing moments saw Chappelle wandering the stage with a cigarette in hand while Stone embraced Butler, her Eddington costar.

Though Jordan and Butler didn't appear in any sketches, their presence may have to do with the fact that Goggins also stars in Miami Vice '85 and may have invited them along to witness the fun. Deadline previously reported that Goggins fills a villainous role in the reboot, as a henchman of the cartel king played by John Leguizamo.

Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter .

Jordan and Butler are set to take over the classic roles of detective duo Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett in the movie reboot based on the popular 1980s TV series. Philip Michael Thomas and Don Johnson starred as Tubbs and Crockett in the original crime drama, a pair of Metro-Dade Police Department detectives working undercover in Miami, Fla. The new film, inspired by the pilot episode and first season of the series, will explore the "glamour and corruption of mid-80s Miami."

articles.summary: "American Idol" alum Justin Guarini opens up about the dark spiral after RCA dropped him and how embracing failure led to Broadway, "Wicked" and a whole new identity.
articles.body: At the start of his career, Justin Guarini seemed to have it all: fame, fortune and a promising future in Hollywood. After becoming the runner-up on the first season of "American Idol" in 2002, Guarini was thrust into the spotlight seemingly overnight. But when his Hollywood dream came crashing down, he found himself in a dark place that he would eventually come to view as one of his greatest blessings. "I think it was one of the greatest things that could ever have happened to me," Guarini, who recently released his book, "Center Stage Confidence: How to Own Your Story and Command Any Room," told Fox News Digital. "Failure is the greatest teacher, one of the greatest teachers that we can have in any given situation because in that failure, you have one of two paths. You either give up or you keep going." TAYLOR HICKS CREDITS FAITH AND BLUE-COLLAR BIRMINGHAM ROOTS FOR KEEPING HIM GROUNDED AFTER 'AMERICAN IDOL' WIN However, this mindset didn't sink in until much later. In his book, Guarini recalled the moment he learned he had been dropped by his record label, RCA, in 2003. "I stared at the TV in shock as my entire world came crumbling down around my ears," Guarini, who said he learned the news during a "Weekend Update" segment on "Saturday Night Live," wrote in his book. "Every illusion of fame, fortune, and glory fell away in an instant — only to be replaced by the silence of loss. In that moment, the veil of my arrogance, my assumptions, and my entitlement were lifted away, and I saw my life for what it had become." "I lost weight, slept more and more, and became less and less like myself, and the people who loved me started to notice and worry. 'GOLDBERGS’ STAR JEFF GARLIN SAYS HE PLANNED TO TAKE HIS OWN LIFE AMID TURBULENT FINAL DAYS ON SITCOM As the first runner-up in "Idol" history, Guarini believed his future in the entertainment industry was secure. WATCH: 'AMERICAN IDOL' STAR JUSTIN GUARINI ENDURED DARK SPIRAL AFTER HOLLYWOOD DREAM COLLAPSED As his career stalled, Guarini struggled to reconcile his newfound reality with the life he had envisioned. KELLY CLARKSON WON’T LET HER KIDS WATCH ‘FROM JUSTIN TO KELLY’ AFTER BRUTAL ADMISSION ABOUT 2003 FILM "There have been plenty of people who've given up and failed and found other things," Guarini told Fox News Digital. COUNTRY STAR GABBY BARRETT SAYS SHE 'SLEPT IN THE CAR' BEFORE 'AMERICAN IDOL' CHANGED HER LIFE "I realized that there were still people celebrating me," he said. After independently releasing his second album in 2005, Guarini found opportunities in television before making his Broadway debut in "Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown" in 2010. He went on to appear in several Broadway productions, including "American Idiot," "Romeo and Juliet" and "Wicked." In 2015, he introduced audiences to another side of his talent when he began portraying Lil' Sweet, the flamboyant character featured in Diet Dr Pepper advertising campaigns. articles.title: Soul Glo’s Diaspora Problems is a hardcore record like no other
articles.summary: Philly’s premiere hardcore band, Soul Glo, put out one of the 21st century’s best punk albums: Diaspora Problems.
articles.body: Soul Glo has a new record called NA I’M GON GRAB ALLAT coming out in January, and I, for one, can not wait. While two singles have dropped, it’s not enough to truly tide me over, so I’ve been revisiting Songs to Yeet at the Sun and my favorite album of 2022 — Diaspora Problems. “Gold Chain Punk (whogonbeatmyass?)” is an opening salvo for the ages. Bong rip, into a catchy-as-hell hardcore riff, with frontman Pierce Jordan ranting. Then comes the half-time stomp as Jordan gets fully unhinged, screaming “Who gon beat my ass? Who the fuck gon beat my ass?” From here on out, as the music shifts through a few different sections, the energy never comes down. Jordan shreds his vocal cords, begging, “Can I live?” Before finally spelling it out for anyone still confused: > Say more, say less, it’s all the same When it’s time to die we can meet outside To see who gon feel my pain [Media: The record barely lets up from here on out. “Coming Correct” opens with a cough and a steady 808, giving you literally three seconds to catch your breath before Jordan jumps on the mic shouting, “I try to listen the way, I wanna be listened to.” The song starts stacking elements quickly, reaching full firestorm by 25 seconds in, and then does let up for the rest of its three-minute runtime. The front chunk of the record is just perfect unrelenting hardcore song after perfect unrelenting hardcore song. Jordan’s crazed charisma is undeniable as he ricochets between leftist rhetoric, goofy bits about smoking weed, and vulnerable explorations of his struggles with depression. You’d be forgiven for struggling to keep up with his rapid-fire delivery, which owes almost as much to modern rappers as it does to classic hardcore acts like Minor Threat or Bad Brains. Track six, “Driponomics,” fully embraces those more modern influences with trap snares, wall-rattling 808 kicks, and a guest verse from Mother Maryrose. The sampled guitar calls to mind the sax squeals favored by the Bomb Squad… just heavier. The album eventually culminates in “Spiritual Level Of Gang Shit,” which features guest verses from McKinley Dixon and Lojii over gently echoed guitar melodies and dub-inspired groove. Then, around the 2:20 mark, things take a turn as the guitars turn punishing and the drums shift to a standard hardcore beat. But the song hasn’t reached its final form yet. That comes almost a minute later when the horn section kicks in. Next to other modern hardcore standard bearers like Turnstile, Soul Glo might almost seem like traditionalists heavily influenced by the DC scene. But Diaspora Problems shows their ambition and willingness to take risks. Soul Glo plays with genre, is confrontational in its politics, and is generally just uncompromising. Oh, and they put on a hell of a live show (I’ve seen them at least four times now). Don’t miss their incredible Tiny Desk Concert either, which I’m pretty sure is the first mosh pit to even open up in the NPR offices. articles.title: Celina Leão: desafios na saúde, educação e BRB no governo do DF | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo começa com série de cobranças à administração pública que ainda aguardam respostas. G1 reuniu principais problemas que a governadora terá pela frente no mandato que vai até 2030.
articles.summary: A governadora Celina Leão inicia novo ciclo no governo do DF com a missão de sanar a crise no BRB e resolver problemas críticos na saúde e na educação básica.
articles.body:
Governadora do DF, Celina Leão (PP) — Foto: TV Globo/Reprodução

Reeleita para governar o Distrito Federal pelos próximos quatro anos, Celina Leão (PP) terá desafios em múltiplas áreas.

O novo ciclo de governo começa com uma série de cobranças à administração pública que ainda aguardam respostas — da crise na saúde à situação financeira do BRB, passando pelos desafios na relação com o Poder Executivo e pelos problemas nas áreas de educação e cultura.

O g1 reuniu os principais problemas que a governadora terá pela frente no mandato que vai até 2030 em uma série de reportagens . Veja abaixo:

Os desafios não têm apenas relação temática: são ligados diretamente . Isso, porque o próprio governo do DF reconhece que o BRB precisa de um empréstimo bilionário para se salvar. E, como acionista majoritário, caberia ao próprio governo quitar essa dívida no médio prazo.

Os dois temas, que ganharam peso nas campanhas eleitorais de 2026, devem estar entre as principais questões enfrentadas pela governadora no início da próxima gestão.

Nos últimos anos, reportagens do g1 e da TV Globo mostraram uma rede pública marcada por hospitais e UPAs superlotadas, falta de profissionais, filas para cirurgias e episódios que colocaram em xeque a qualidade da assistência prestada à população.

O ápice da crise ocorreu no primeiro semestre, após uma sequência de mortes investigadas por suspeita de negligência. Celina, que já havia assumido o cargo, reconheceu o sucateamento na estrutura e afirmou que era necessário melhorar o atendimento (veja no vídeo acima).

Embora o governo tenha anunciado medidas para ampliar a capacidade da rede — como a convocação de médicos e a abertura de novas vagas —, hospitais e UPAs continuaram registrando problemas de superlotação e dificuldade para absorver a demanda.

Antes referência nacional, a rede pública de ensino do DF enfrenta um déficit histórico no quadro de profissionais e, desde a pandemia, viu despencar o resultado no Índice de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica (Ideb) – que, neste ano, ficou abaixo da média nacional.

Celina trocou o comando da Secretaria de Educação e em agosto, Iêdes Braga – secretária nomeada ainda na gestão Ibaneis Rocha (MDB) – foi substituída por Thiago Peixoto.

Medidas adotadas pelo novo secretário de Educação, em poucos meses, já têm causado atritos entre o governo e o Sindicato dos Professores no Distrito Federal (Sinpro-DF).

Em 21 de outubro, quatro dias antes do segundo turno, a entidade convocou paralisação contra o que classificou como autoritarismo. Entre as medidas, o Sinpro destacou o envio de materiais didáticos escolhidos sem a participação da categoria e imposição de um novo calendário escolar.

Celina Leão (PP), governadora do DF, e Lula (PT), presidente do Brasil — Foto: reprodução

O segundo turno das eleições deste ano renovou o mandato de Celina no governo do DF – e também o mandato de Lula (PT) na Presidência da República.

O resultado mantém ativo o desafio que atravessa a relação institucional entre os dois níveis de governo desde 2023 – e que se intensificou ao longo deste ano. Apenas em 2026, Celina Leão:

se apresentou como aliada de Flávio Bolsonaro e fez oposição a Lula;

tentou acordos com o governo Federal para salvar o Banco de Brasília (BRB), mas recebeu críticas do presidente Lula;

acionou o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) para tentar anular uma lei sancionada por Lula que, segundo o processo, pode afetar repasses do governo federal ao DF.

Para o professor Frederico Bertholini, do Instituto de Ciência Política da Universidade de Brasília, o desafio central de Celina é separar a relação institucional da disputa eleitoral .

A relação do governo do DF com o setor cultural, em 2026, foi marcada até aqui por uma sequência de críticas e problemas graves de subfinanciamento, adiamentos e pressões.

Desde que Celina Leão assumiu a chefia do Executivo local, os episódios se acumularam : impasses com o Fundo de Apoio à Cultura, atraso nos repasses ao Cine Brasília e o quase cancelamento do 59º Festival de Cinema.

Reeleita pelos próximos quatro anos, Celina afirmou ao g1 que pretende "intensificar as políticas culturais em todas as regiões do DF, fortalecer o Fundo de Apoio à Cultura e as bibliotecas da capital".

articles.title: Donna Mills on why she never married despite decades-long romance: 'I was always so independent'
articles.summary: Donna Mills reveals why she and Larry Gilman never married despite 25 years together, citing her fierce independence and a practical approach to love.
articles.body: "Knots Landing" star Donna Mills is revealing the reason that she has never walked down the aisle despite her 25-year romance with actor Larry Gilman. During a recent appearance on the "Still Here Hollywood Podcast with Steve Kmetko," the 85-year-old actress, who has been in a relationship with Gilman, 76, since 2001, opened up about why she has chosen to avoid marriage. "I was always so independent," she told Kmetko. "I’m still very independent." RITA WILSON IGNORED HER MOTHER'S OLD-SCHOOL MARRIAGE ADVICE, AND IT LED HER TO TOM HANKS "I just didn’t ever want to be subject to whatever you have to do when you get married," Mills continued. "I also didn’t want to say I was going to love somebody forever." "I don’t know if I would do that or not," she admitted with a laugh. ‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH LIVED APART FROM HER HUSBAND FOR 17 YEARS DURING THEIR 35-YEAR LOVE STORY Mills shared the topic of marriage had also come up between herself and her daughter Chloe, who recently tied the knot herself. "It’s funny because my daughter asked me that. My daughter just got married," Mills said. "And she just had a baby." After Kmetko told her that she didn't "look like a grandmother," Mills pointed to a necklace she was wearing that was inscribed with the word "Grandma," which she said was a gift from Chloe. "She gave me this, and I wear it all the time," Mills said. Mills explained that she and Chloe have had many conversations about what name her grandson would call her. "And I said, "'Oh, I know. Glamma,'" Mills told Kmetko with a laugh. "But she didn't like that." The Daytime Emmy Award winner Chloe adopted as a newborn in 1994 when she was 54. Seven years later, Mills began dating Gilman, whom she has described as an "incredibly kind, funny, wonderful man." "I love him," she told The Daily Beast in 2022. "I’m lucky to have found him. I found him late, but I found him. Everybody loves him. He’s great." NICOLE KIDMAN, RACHAEL RAY, TED DANSON KEEP MARRIAGES HOT WITH UNCONVENTIONAL RULES Prior to meeting Gilman, Mills and advertising executive Richard Holland, who was previously married to singer Chaka Khan, had an on-and-off relationship for around 20 years starting in 1979. When asked why she has never married, Mills said, "I don’t remember anyone ever getting down on one knee." TIM MCGRAW WARNS OF ‘MOST DANGEROUS’ TIMES IN MARRIAGE AFTER 30 YEARS WITH FAITH HILL The "Nope" star also cited her independent streak and explained why she and Gilman never felt the need to marry after meeting later in life. "I am so freaking independent. I just am. I’m very independent and by the time Larry and I met we were both pretty established," she said. "To combine everything at that point is really difficult. So we just combined our lives but not our finances and stuff like that. It’s much cleaner, much better." GREAT RELATIONSHIPS HAVE 3 ESSENTIAL INGREDIENTS — AND ONE FACTOR THAT CAN RUIN EVERYTHING Mills shared that maintaining her independence had always given her a sense of security, even while sharing her life with a partner. "I’ve always felt a woman being independent was important," she said. "It made me feel safer, I guess, to know that I can take care of myself. I want someone to be in my life to love and be with, to be a companion and to go places and all that, but if I have to I can take care of myself." "And really, I had enough marriages as Abby!" she added, referring to the character she played on "Knots Landing." Mills became a television sensation playing the glamorous and ruthless Abby Cunningham on "Knots Landing" from 1980 to 1989. Abby tied the knot four times over the course of the hit primetime soap, though one union was annulled almost immediately after the wedding. Mills and Gilman share a home in the Los Angeles neighborhood of Brentwood, where they have a vineyard. In 2015, Mills told Closer Weekly that the vineyard was a gift from her longtime partner. "Larry planted a vineyard for me last year," Donna shared. "He’s really such a good guy." articles.title: Quote of the day by Meryl Streep: ‘Your difference is the most valuable thing you have,’ the 'Devil Wears Prada' star on embracing what makes one unique
articles.summary: Meryl Streep encourages individuals to embrace their uniqueness in a recent quote, highlighting that our differences are our greatest strengths. Discover her empowering advice in this insightful article.
articles.body: Have you ever stopped yourself from saying something because you thought people might find it strange? Or perhaps you've liked something that your friends didn't understand and quietly decided to keep it to yourself. Most people have had moments like these. Sometimes, we spend so much time worrying about how we're coming across that we forget there's nothing particularly wrong with being a little different.Meryl Streep once spoke about this while answering questions from students at a university. The actress had faced her fair share of criticism when she was younger, including comments about her appearance. But rather than treating those differences as things she needed to hide, she had a rather interesting piece of advice for the students listening to her.Today's quote of the day by Meryl Streep reads: “Everyone thinks there’s a perfect way to be … but your difference, your thing that is unique to you, is the most valuable thing you have. The weird thing about you is the thing that makes people remember you. … Whatever is weird about you maybe is your strength.”Streep shared these thoughts during her April 1, 2014 appearance at the University of Massachusetts Lowell. The conversation was later covered in the Summer 2014 issue of UMass Lowell Magazine in an article titled 'Straight Streep', written by Jill Gambon. A student had asked her how she dealt with failure and rejection. Streep spoke about being criticised for her nose and surname early in her career before explaining why she believed people should hold on to the things that make them different.What does the quote by Meryl Streep mean?Think about the things you might hesitate to tell someone when you first meet them. Maybe your music taste is a little unusual, you have an interest nobody around you shares or you're just someone who doesn't always know what to say in a group. These things might seem small, but they can make you feel a little out of place sometimes.Meryl Streep's advice is to stop worrying so much about these differences. You might think a particular quality makes you stand out for the wrong reasons, but someone else could actually find it interesting. There's no real reason to change your personality just because it doesn't match the people around you.She also knows what being judged feels like. When she was starting as an actress, people made comments about her appearance, including her nose. It's something she brought up while speaking to the students, which makes her advice feel much more personal.How is the quote by Meryl Streep relevant today?Keeping up with trends can get tiring, especially when they seem to change every other week. There's always a new style people are trying, a particular way of presenting yourself online or some new idea of what looks good. Before you know it, you might find yourself questioning things you were perfectly happy with a few months ago.It happens in smaller ways, too. You might dress differently around certain friends, avoid talking about something you're interested in or hold back a part of your personality because you're worried about how it'll be received. Most people probably have a few examples of doing this.Meryl Streep's words are a good reminder to think twice before changing things about yourself just to fit in. You won't click with everyone, and some people might not understand your choices. That's part of life. There's no point in making yourself less interesting just to be more likeable to everyone else.Early life of Meryl StreepMeryl Streep was born on June 22, 1949, in Summit, New Jersey, United States. She attended Vassar College and later joined the Yale School of Drama, where she completed her Master of Fine Arts degree.Her interest in acting developed early, and she started performing in theatre before making her way into films. Her time at Yale also gave her formal acting training, which helped prepare her for the roles she would take on later in her career.How did Meryl Streep rise to fame?Meryl Streep's film career began with 'Julia' (1977), followed by 'The Deer Hunter' (1978), which brought her wider recognition. Her role in 'Kramer vs. Kramer' (1979) earned her first Academy Award. She won another just a few years later for 'Sophie's Choice' (1982).Over the years, she's played some very different characters. For many viewers, she'll always be Miranda Priestly from 'The Devil Wears Prada' (2006). Others might remember her as Julia Child in 'Julie & Julia' (2009) or Margaret Thatcher in 'The Iron Lady' (2011), a performance that earned her third Academy Award.Streep has spent decades moving between drama, comedy and biographical films. Even after all these years, she continues to take on roles that are quite different from one another. Her filmography is a good place to start if you want to see just how much range she has as an actress.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Inside the 1920s Los Angeles home of 'Nobody Wants This' fame Erin Foster and her husband Simon Tikhman: A blend of vintage charm and modern design
articles.summary: Explore the beautifully renovated 1920s Los Angeles home of Erin Foster and Simon Tikhman, blending vintage charm with modern design, perfect for family life and entertaining.
articles.body: Not every celebrity home is a museum, and Erin Foster and Simon Tikhman’s definitely isn’t. They wanted a place where friends could hang out, their daughter could run around, and daily life could feel easy. The result, in Los Angeles, pairs historic architecture with colourful interiors and smart technology, and it’s elegant without trying too hard.Foster, the creator of 'Nobody Wants This,' and Tikhman, a music executive, worked with interior designer Joyce Pickens Dinwiddy of JDP Interiors on a four-year renovation, according to Architectural Digest. The aim was to make the 1920s house feel cosy, playful and personal.A historic home with a mix of influencesThe house brings together Spanish, Mediterranean Revival and English design influences. Rather than sticking to one style, the couple embraced elements of all three, giving the property a distinctive character.The entrance sets the tone. The foyer was opened up to feel roomier the moment you step inside, and decorative tiles and a vintage mirror add a touch of history. The couple wanted a grand-looking entrance, but one that would still feel inviting to visitors.A living room designed for conversationsThe living room is among the home's most welcoming spaces. Custom sofas are arranged to encourage conversation, while a vintage chair, patterned upholstery and a statement chandelier bring personality to the interiors.Foster describes it as the room where she enjoys inviting friends over for drinks. Custom furniture, vintage finds and carefully chosen fabrics make the space feel collected rather than overly coordinated. It reflects the couple’s wish for a home that looks beautiful but stays comfortable enough for everyday life.A green kitchen and a sunlit solariumGreen is one of Foster’s favourite colours, and in the kitchen it takes centre stage. The cabinets are painted in Denali Green, paired with floral fabric and hand-painted backsplash tiles. A copper range hood adds warmth to the space.Tikhman also requested a separate refrigerator for drinks, which Foster jokingly compared to a Kardashian-style fridge.Another highlight is the glass-ceilinged breakfast nook, known as the solarium. The structure was brought into the house by crane, making it one of the more ambitious additions to the renovation. With slate-blue walls and a custom seating arrangement, the room provides a bright setting for morning coffee, work and early dinners with their daughter, Noa.Traditional design meets modern technologyThe dining room pairs a custom table and chairs with a vintage chandelier and a Danish sideboard. Elsewhere, a bar and a separate lounge area reflect Tikhman's preferences. He jokingly calls the solarium his “man cave,” a small sign of how the couple made room for both of their tastes.The primary bedroom is all about comfort, with soft fabrics, custom lighting and muted wall colours. In the bathroom, a hand-painted mural and vintage marble tiles add decorative touches.Technology is another important part of the property. Tikhman, cofounder and CEO of The Core Entertainment, wanted a smart home without making gadgets dominate the interiors. Speakers are built into the walls, a dining-room mirror conceals a television, and an AI assistant named Nicola controls lighting, temperature and music.A family home made for entertainingFor Foster and Tikhman, the house is not meant to be a space where guests feel uncomfortable. They enjoy hosting Shabbat dinners and welcoming friends and their children. Speaking to Architectural Digest, Foster explained that she does not want an untouchable home where visitors worry about leaving a mark or making themselves comfortable.The garden and swimming pool extend the entertaining space outdoors. Their daughter Noa’s bedroom has been designed with the future in mind, since Foster plans to adapt it as Noa’s personality and interests grow.The couple’s Los Angeles home pulls together several design ideas without losing its warmth. From the colourful kitchen and conversation-friendly living room to the hidden technology and welcoming outdoor spaces, every area reflects their shared approach to family life. It’s a reminder that a beautiful home doesn’t have to feel like a museum. articles.title: Russell Brand facing significant prison term for rape and sexual assaults
articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand faces a reckoning Monday for sexual abuse that occurred just offstage from a public life built around boasts of his erotic exploi...
articles.body:
The top photos of the day by AP's photojournalists

LONDON (AP) — Russell Brand faces a reckoning Monday for sexual abuse that occurred just offstage from a public life built around boasts of his erotic exploits.

Brand, 51, faces a significant prison term after being convicted of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.

The British actor-comedian known for outrageous stand-up routines and battles with drugs and alcohol asserted that he was innocent and all his encounters were consensual.

But a jury of eight men and four women did not buy his defense and found him guilty of attacking four of six accusers on allegations dating back to 2004. He was cleared of two counts of rape and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Brand was partly damned by his own words about his obsession with sex and his well-documented life of promiscuity.

Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones called Brand a ruthless, calculating, manipulative "sexual predator" who treated women as a "disposable commodity."

She quoted from his 2007 memoir "My Booky Wook" to illustrate how his insatiable sex drive led him to cross the line.

"If I want something — whether it's a job or a woman — I will determinedly, resolutely, remove anything that's in the way, until I possess the object of my desire," he wrote.

The accusers came forward following a 2023 investigation by The Times and Channel 4 that aired accusations from women who said they had been sexually abused and degraded by Brand .

Brand was convicted of sexually assaulting a woman during a birthday party at a London bar in 2004, but cleared of orally raping her in a restroom.

He was also found guilty of kissing and groping another woman at a London radio station in 2004 or 2005 and of anally raping a fan at his home after meeting her backstage at one of his comedy shows in 2009.

The final conviction was for sexually assaulting a different woman who says the comedian demanded a massage and pressed his face into her groin during the recording of an advertisement in 2009.

Brand was acquitted of raping another woman in a hotel room during the Labour Party's annual conference in the seaside town of Bournemouth in 1999, and of attempting to indecently assault a woman by dragging her into the men's bathroom at the London office of music channel MTV.

The Associated Press doesn't name victims of alleged sexual violence, and British law protects their identities from the media for life.

Brand, who was known for edgy stand-up routines and battles with drugs and alcohol, rose to prominence in the early 2000s hosting television programs and his own BBC radio show. He appeared in Hollywood films including "Forgetting Sarah Marshall" and "Get Him to the Greek" and was briefly married to pop star Katy Perry.

In recent years he has moved away from mainstream media, relocated to Florida and built a large online following with videos mixing wellness, conspiracy theories and discussions of his religious devotion.

articles.title: Inside Daler Mehndi’s farmhouse: A look at the singer’s reported properties in Haryana and Delhi
articles.summary: Daler Mehndi, known for popularising Punjabi pop and Bhangra internationally, has been associated with substantial land holdings in Haryana.
articles.body: Daler Mehndi, known for popularising Punjabi pop and Bhangra internationally, has been associated with substantial land holdings in Haryana. The singer's reported properties in and around Sohna, near Gurugram, have also drawn attention over the years. While one farmhouse is linked to environmental violations, another reportedly faced municipal action in 2013.According to a Hindustan Times report, the singer owns a farmhouse in Sohna, located around 25 kilometres from Gurugram. Reports have also attributed approximately 112 acres of land in the region to him. Details about the properties include a farmhouse near Damdama Lake and an earlier 10-acre estate that became part of a municipal action.Farmhouse located near Damdama LakeOne property associated with Daler Mehndi is a 1.5-acre farmhouse near Damdama Lake in Sohna. The property is situated in the Aravalli region, which is known for its natural surroundings. Its location also places it relatively close to the rapidly developing Gurugram area.However, the farmhouse has reportedly faced action from local authorities over alleged environmental violations. The Gurugram district administration and the Department of Town and Country Planning (DTCP) sealed the property. The action was reportedly taken over violations of regulations associated with the National Green Tribunal (NGT).The 2013 action involving a 10-acre farmhouseDaler Mehndi was previously linked to a land dispute in Sohna that came into focus in 2013. During that period, the Sohna Municipal Council took possession of his reported 10-acre farmhouse. The operation was carried out with police assistance.The action was part of a larger effort by the authorities to reclaim hundreds of acres of farmland allegedly occupied by influential individuals. The municipal council acted following directions from the sub-divisional magistrate.Dispute over village common landThe wider case involved approximately 1,900 acres of shamlat deh, which refers to village common land. The land had allegedly been transferred to private parties through irregularities involving revenue department officials. Some buyers later sold the plots to prominent individuals and real estate developers at substantial prices.The Sohna Municipal Council had filed a case under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act in June 2011. The proceedings targeted properties allegedly built or occupied on land that had been transferred unlawfully. Daler Mehndi's reported farmhouse was among the properties covered by the action.Another property reference in West DelhiDaler Mehndi has also been mentioned in references connected to Nihal Vihar, Chander Vihar and Khushi Ram Park in Nangloi, West Delhi. However, these references do not establish the existence of an active farmhouse or a current residential estate belonging to the singer in that locality.According to Just Dial information, the area is associated with neighbourhood businesses, including small shops and eateries around 50-foot Road. Therefore, the West Delhi connection should be treated separately from the reported properties in Sohna. The available details do not confirm ownership of a celebrity estate at this location.Daler Mehndi's career and recent musical projectsBorn on August 18, 1967, in Patna, Bihar, Daler Mehndi grew up in a Punjabi Sikh family. He formed a musical group in 1991 with his brothers, cousins and friends. His career received international recognition in 1994 when he won the Voice of Asia International Ethnic and Pop Music Contest in Almaty, Kazakhstan.He subsequently became known for his energetic stage performances, distinctive turban and flowing robes. His music played an important role in taking Punjabi pop beyond the traditional Bollywood sound.In 2026, his musical releases have included the devotional track 'Dukaalan Pranaase' and the Punjabi song 'Daule', featuring music by Gurmeet Singh. He has also been associated with promotional musical work connected to upcoming film projects, including 'Welcome to the Jungle'.DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ stomps to a record-setting $31.6 debut, clobbering ‘The Cat in the Hat’
articles.summary: “Godzilla Minus Zero” stomped into movie theaters with a chart-topping $31.6 million over the weekend, scoring a record debut for a foreign-language film at the North American box office.
articles.body: NEW YORK — “Godzilla Minus Zero” stomped into movie theaters with a chart-topping $31.6 million over the weekend, scoring a record debut for a foreign-language film at the North American box office. Takashi Yamazaki’s sequel to 2023’s Oscar-winning “Godzilla Minus One” easily thrashed Warner Bros.’ animated “The Cat in the Hat” movie. That film, featuring the voice of Bill Hader, opened with $20.5 million, according to studio estimates Sunday, plus $10 million overseas. While Godzilla recently celebrated his 72nd birthday, Yamazaki has revived one of the longest running franchises in movies by bringing the series back to its Japanese roots. The film, produced by Toho and distributed in North America by GKids, is set in post-WWII Japan. No live-action foreign language film has had a bigger opening weekend, unless you count 2004’s “Passion of the Christ,” which opened with $83.8 million despite its largely Aramaic dialogue. Last year, the anime “Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle” debuted with $70.6 million. But “Godzilla Minus Zero” bested the mark for live-action previously held by 2004’s “Hero” (a $17.9 million launch) and added to the trend of international, non-English productions drawing American audiences to cinemas. Japanese and Indian films score in North America The weekend also saw the widest North American release for an Indian film. “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, is a Hindi-language epic of Indian mythology that, as part one of two, is the most expensive Indian film ever made. Distributed by Sony Pictures in North America, it launched with $8.7 million domestically and $32 million in India. “Godzilla Minus Zero” and “Ramayana” were both given global releases, debuting in their home countries at the same time as they reached American audiences. In Japan, “Godzilla Minus Zero” grossed about $17 million over the weekend. “This historic opening shows how deeply audiences around the world connect with Godzilla and with Takashi Yamazaki’s vision,” said Koji Ueda, president of Toho Global, in a statement. “Our first near-simultaneous global release was built on that belief.” “Godzilla Minus One,” which won the Oscar for best visual effects, was the highest-grossing Japanese live-action film ever in U.S. and Canada despite a modest budget under $15 million. “Godzilla Minus Zero,” carrying a budget of less than $20 million, is sure to blow past its predecessor’s record haul of $57.1 million. Since first premiering last month at the New York Film Festival, the film has scored well with critics (90% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes) and audiences (an “A” CinemaScore). “Godzilla” and “Ramayana” were each filmed for IMAX, with Yamazaki’s film receiving an early IMAX-only release on Tuesday. Both benefited greatly from large-format screens. “Godzilla Minus Zero” generated $21.3 million globally, or 34% of its box-office take, from IMAX. The big result for “Godzilla Minus Zero” will either whet audiences’ appetites or pose an awkward comparison for the next Hollywood, English-language Godzilla movie. In March, Warner Bros. and Legendary will release “Godzilla x Kong: Supernova.” ‘The Cat in the Hat’ disappoints, ‘Drummer Boy’ overperforms “The Cat in the Hat” was the latest attempt to revive the Dr. Seuss classic on the big screen, following the Mike Myers-led 2003 live-action film. But the animated “Cat in the Hat,” made for $86 million, drummed up only modest interest from moviegoers. Reviews (44% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes) were bad. Not helping “The Cat in the Hat”: Laika’s acclaimed stop motion animated fantasy “Wildwood” has held well with audiences, even briefly leading all films at the box office early in the week. “Wildwood” dipped just 22% in its third weekend, with $7 million. With a cumulative total of $39.8 million domestically, it’s fared well, even if Travis Knight’s pricey passion project, with a budget of at least $100 million, is all but certain to lose tens of millions. Third place went to Angel Studios’ “Drummer Boy,” with $9.3 million on its opening weekend. The Revolutionary War-set musical also saw its music top the iTunes chart. Led by ‘Wild Horse Nine,’ Oscar contenders surge One of the weekend’s biggest successes was “Wild Horse Nine,” Martin McDonagh’s dark comedy about a pair of CIA officers (John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell) on Easter Island. It opened with $6 million domestic and $6.6 million internationally, a stellar result for an awards movie and a personal best for McDonagh. Since its premiere at the Venice Film Festival, “Wild Horse Nine” has been seen as a top Oscar contender, and its reception from audiences will boost that cause. The film, a Searchlight Pictures release, launched in 1,100 domestic theaters, a number that will roughly double next weekend. Another pair of potential Oscar contenders got off to good starts in limited release. Jordan Firstman’s “Club Kid,” about a gay New York party boy who finds out he has a son, debuted with a $65,097 theater average from six screens for A24. “I Play Rocky,” Peter Farrelly’s comic telling of the making of “Rocky,” launched with a $49,200 per-screen average from seven theaters for Amazon MGM Studios. Meanwhile, Nathan Fiedler and Lance Oppenheim’s “You Can See Everything” continued its sensational run, grossing $8.9 million in its fourth weekend of release. The A24 documentary about Elizabeth Holmes has so far collected $79.8 million in North America. After a sleepy Halloween weekend at the box office, overall ticket sales were up a whopping 96.8% from the previous weekend, according to Rentrak. Top 10 movies by domestic box office With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak: 1. “Godzilla Minus Zero,” $31.6 million. 2. “The Cat in the Hat,” $20.5 million. 3. “Drummer Boy,” $9.3 million. 4. “You Can See Everything,” $8.9 million. 5. “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” $8.7 million. 6. “Wildwood,” $7 million. 7. “Clayface,” $6.7 million. 8. “Wild Horse Nine,” $6 million. 9. Stray Kids live viewing, $3.7 million. 10. “Wicker,” $3.4 million.

articles.title: Suriya rules out political entry, says, 'I am quietly watching politics' at 'Scene' success meet
articles.summary: Actor Suriya has cleared the air about his political entry, saying he has no plans to join politics.
articles.body: Actor Suriya has cleared the air about his political entry, saying he has no plans to join politics. His remarks come at a time when several actors are being linked to political ambitions in Tamil Nadu following Chief Minister Vijay's entry into politics. Suriya, who has been actively involved in educational initiatives through his Agaram Foundation, has often been discussed as a potential political face because of his social work and fan following.Suriya's political entry clarificationSpeaking at an event related to his Diwali release 'Scene' in Chennai on November 8, Suriya directly addressed questions about his political future. “I am not going to enter politics. That does not mean I hate politics. I am quietly and closely watching politics,” he said, as reported by Cinema Vikatan. The actor also stressed that he would never enter politics without understanding the field properly. “I will not enter politics even without knowing the way,” Suriya added, putting an end to speculation about an immediate political move. He further explained that anyone who genuinely wishes to serve people can enter politics, provided they understand its challenges and responsibilities.Suriya says real change begins with knowledgeDuring the interaction, Suriya also shared his thoughts on education, corruption and social change. He said education was the key to addressing several problems faced by society and stressed that political leaders should give it greater importance. “Corruption cannot be eliminated by a third person. Every individual must fight that battle within themselves,” he said. The actor also explained that the work carried out through Agaram Foundation was not intended to serve any political purpose. “I will not call the work we do a service. It is our responsibility,” he stated, highlighting his commitment to helping students access education.Suriya's 'Scene' Diwali release and successOn the other hand, his latest movie titled 'Scene', released during Diwali, has become a very big topic of discussion. articles.title: ‘Ramayana’ designer delivered Ranbir Kapoor’s armor an hour before shoot: 'He liked my work'
articles.summary: 'Ramayana: Part 1', directed by Nitesh Tiwari, required extensive research, fine craftsmanship and strong collaboration between its cast and technical
articles.body: 'Ramayana: Part 1', directed by Nitesh Tiwari, required extensive research, fine craftsmanship and strong collaboration between its cast and technical team to build its visual world. Costume and armor designer Ajay Kumar found perfecting Ranbir Kapoor’s armor as Lord Rama to be one of his biggest challenges. He has now spoken about how the actor’s inputs shaped the final look, why the fitting became a race against time and how he approached designing the armor for Yash’s Ravana.'Ramayana' designer Ajay Kumar on the challenge of the first armorIn a conversation with Variety India, Kumar spoke about the difficulty of making the princely armor Kapoor wears in the first half of the film. He said, “I have been in this industry for 15 years but not as an armor designer. The most challenging was to deliver the first armor. My sample had a thickness of 8mm to 10mm, but the final product had to have a thickness of 2mm to 4mm. It was very tough because it was made of rubber, which took two weeks.”The process got even tougher once Ranbir gave his feedback. He wanted the armor to look more refined and sit snugly against his body, without jutting out from the shoulder or neckline. Kumar reveals, “Ranbir also gave his feedback. He told me I did exactly what he was looking for, but he wanted it to be refined. He wanted the armour to be fitted to the skin and away from the shoulder or neckline. I got the same feedback from Ravie Dubey (Lakshman).”Designer delivers the armor an hour before the shootThe designer was left with only two days to make the changes and ended up delivering the armor just an hour before the shoot. He adds, “I went to RK’s vanity and requested him to try his armor on. He kept trusting me with the whole process, and it was important for me to make him feel like Ram in the clothes. I was scared because everything depended on how the armor was. Then he tried it on and gave me a go-ahead. He liked my work.”About 'Ramayana: Part 1'Directed by Nitesh Tiwari, the film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Yash as Ravana, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravie Dubey as Laxman, Arun Govil as King Dashrath, Indira Krishnan as Kaushalya, Lara Dutta as Kaikeyi, Sheeba Chaddha as Manthara, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha and Kajal Aggarwal as Mandodari.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
